source.title: Stochastic Gradient Flow Dynamics of Test Risk and its Exact Solution for Weak Features
source.authors: Rodrigo Veiga; Anastasia Remizova; Nicolas Macris

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and evaluates test-risk curves in a weak-features regression model, using gradient-flow and stochastic-gradient-flow dynamics rather than only the static least-squares estimator.
record.gate_note: The paper's own weak-features risk results are recorded. Results attributed to cited work are not rows. It reports time-dependent risk, but does not test a fall-rise-fall curve over training time at fixed model size.
record.test_reason: The paper's main contribution is the SGF correction, but it also derives and plots its own GF test-risk curves for the weak-features linear regression model (Eq. 31, Fig. 5a). These show risk falling again past the interpolation threshold α=1 in a non-deep model class, and this was checked against GD simulations. The t→∞ limit re-derives the least-squares double-descent curve of Belkin, Hsu & Xu (2020). The new element is the finite-time and stochastic dynamics, so this is a new-setting test of V4 only.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The paper derives a path-integral formula for the SGF-minus-GF test-risk difference and computes it exactly in the weak-features double-descent model. The authors report good agreement with SGD simulations, note the approach is heuristic and applied only to a simple model, and highlight that the infinite-time stochastic correction exists only below the interpolation threshold.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the weak-features regression setting associated with prior double-descent work, but evaluates finite-time GF and SGF dynamics and their test-risk correction rather than only the static least-squares estimator.
record.method_sensitivity: The SGF-minus-GF risk correction varies with α and time; the reported theory is less accurate at intermediate times and has finite-size discrepancies, particularly below the interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: At infinite time the SGF-minus-GF test-risk correction is nonzero only for α<1 and vanishes for α>1. At finite times its maximum shifts from above to below the threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the weak-features model, SGD noise raises test risk only in the underparametrized regime at long training times.

fits_no_version.finding: Early stopping under GF is beneficial for most tested α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In weak-features regression, early stopping improves on the converged least-squares risk for most feature-to-sample ratios.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code is available in “this repository” but gives no URL in the text.
record.problems: The path-integral/Laplace analysis is described as heuristic. The diffusion covariance uses an approximation that neglects O(n^-2) terms. The authors report underestimation at intermediate times, visible finite-size effects, and discrepancies near the interpolation threshold.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for cited prior results. Figures 2–7 contain additional plotted points and parameter curves, but the recorded rows capture the reported risk-curve findings and the stated differences across α and time; individual plot coordinates are not tabulated.

untested.parts: No deep networks; the model is linear regression on a random subset of features.
Risk over training time is plotted (Fig. 5b), but no fall-rise-fall trajectory at fixed α is reported.
Sample size is not varied at fixed model size.
Only one model class, weak-features linear regression; no comparison across classes and no classical U-shaped first descent.
The noise level μ is a parameter, but the peak's dependence on noise or regularization is not studied. Early stopping is noted as beneficial, but whether it removes the peak is not quantified.

missing.what: Finite-time GF risk-vs-α curves showing how the double-descent peak emerges with training time (t/γ from 0 to ∞). These would show whether the peak is absent at early times.

record.verdict_notes: The double-descent curve here is a re-derivation of the known least-squares result in [2], used as a testbed. The evidence for V4 is therefore confirmatory and limited to one linear model class. The degenerate first descent means the classical U-shape is not reproduced. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: The model is a weak-features regression model, not a deep network.
The paper reports risk over time and discusses the emergence of double descent with time, but does not test whether risk at fixed model size follows a fall-rise-fall curve over training time.
It varies the number of learned features relative to sample size; it does not test increasing sample size near a fixed interpolation threshold.
Tests double descent in the weak-features regression setting; it does not test the claim across other model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, and sample axes.
The risk formulas include a label-noise parameter, but the paper does not test whether noise drives or splits peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes them.
The paper does not compare the curve against an effective parameter count.

conditions.value: GF; t→∞ for the limiting curve

rows.value: The asymptotic risk is given by Eq. (31); the t→∞ limit agrees with the double-descent curve. Appendix E describes the limiting double descent as having a degenerate first descent.
rows.note: The plotted curve is also shown at finite time in Fig. 5(a); the authors state that the limiting picture has a degenerate first descent.
rows.check: The second descent past α=1 is observed. The authors state the limiting curve has a 'degenerate first descent', so no classical U-shaped first part appears. The t→∞ curve reproduces the cited result of [2] rather than being new. The finite-time curves in Fig. 5(a) are the paper's own contribution.

rows.subject: weak features model
rows.size_stated: p learned components; asymptotic p/n→α and d/n→ψ
rows.operation_detail: Sweep α and compute the infinite-time SGF-minus-GF test-risk correction.
rows.measure: difference in test risk, SGF minus GF
rows.value: Eq. (34): the correction is γ′/(4ψ) times [(α/ψ)(1−α/ψ)+μ² max(1−α,0)]; the text says it is present for α<1 and absent for α>1.
rows.note: The figure also compares the theoretical correction with discrete-time SGD-minus-GD simulations averaged over 1000 random subsets.
rows.check: This is the SGF-minus-GF correction, not test risk against capacity. It bears on no version, so the link to none is correct.

rows.subject: weak features model
rows.operation_detail: Report the GF test-risk trajectory over time for multiple α values.
rows.measure: average test risk over training time
rows.value: The time-evolution curves are shown in Fig. 5(b); the authors state that early stopping is beneficial for most α values.
rows.note: This reports time-dependent risk, but does not establish a fall-rise-fall trajectory over time at fixed model size.
rows.check: The row shows time evolution of GF risk, with early stopping beneficial for most α. No fall-rise-fall shape over time is stated, so it cannot bear on V2. The state is better recorded as cannot_determine than as observed.

rows.stage_stated: SGF compared with GF; training time t varied
rows.operation_detail: Report how the SGF-minus-GF test-risk difference varies with α and time.

conditions.value: p/n; values shown below and above 1

rows.measure: difference in test risk, SGF minus GF
rows.value: Figures 3 and 4 show the time-dependent difference. The authors state that its maximum is above the interpolation threshold at early times and below it at later times; at intermediate times the theory underestimates the SGD difference. They also describe a knee near the onset of double descent.
rows.note: The plotted values are not tabulated.
rows.check: The SGF-minus-GF difference over time and α is a related construct, not the risk curve itself. The link to none is correct.

relationships.condition: Weak-features Gaussian linear regression, GF at long or infinite training time, ψ=2.5
relationships.reason: Test risk peaks at α=1 and falls again for α>1 (Eq. 31, Fig. 5a), with GD simulations close to theory (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Test risk peaked at α=1 and declined for α>1, with gradient-descent simulations close to theory.

relationships.condition: Same model, finite training time under GF
relationships.reason: From the text: authors describe 'the emergence of the double descent with time' and early stopping helping most α. The peak thus depends on training length, though the rows do not quantify this (R1, Fig. 5a/b).
relationships.display_finding: Double descent emerged over time, and early stopping improved risk for most α values.
